name: CORTEX · LLM-hRIC
title: LLM-Empowered Hierarchical RIC for Intent-Driven Network Slicing on OAI
authors: Lingyan Bao, Seungmin Sim, Wonjoon Lee, and Jemin Lee
summary: LLM-empowered hierarchical RIC for intent-driven PRB allocation across 5G network slices. A Gemma-based Non-RT rApp reasons over operator intents and network states to generate A1 policies, and a Near-RT TD3 controller refines the PRB allocation. End-to-end validation: OAI 5G SA testbed with FlexRIC (E2SM-RC/KPM), two slices, and five UEs, real-time throughput and SLA monitoring.

name: CORTEX · Anti-Jamming dApp
title: dApp–xApp Closed Loop for Real-Time Jamming Mitigation in an OCUDU Testbed
authors: Ngo Van Tuan, Lingyan Bao, Nguyen Thanh Tam, Ngo Van Mao, Binbin Chen, Tony Quek, and Jemin Lee
org: Yonsei University / Singapore University of Technology and Design
summary: Real-time uplink jamming detection with a GPU interference-detection dApp on the OCUDU gNB. dApp + xApp closed loop: the NeuroRAN Near-RT RIC xApp turns jammed PRBs into slot-level PRB masks, and the gNB scheduler applies them to new PUSCH grants. Live 5G SA testbed: GPU-accelerated OCUDU gNB, Sera O-RU, Open5GS core, a 5G dongle and an interference source inside an RF shield box.

name: CORTEX · MT-JAS
title: DRL-Based Joint Advanced Sleep Mode and Network Slicing Control on OAI/FlexRIC
authors: Lingyan Bao, Seong-Lyun Kim, and Jemin Lee
summary: Two-timescale control: a Transformer-based PPO xApp on FlexRIC sets slice PRB quotas and target RU sleep depth per control interval. Slot-level MAC execution: a buffer-aware ASM executor gates PDSCH, while a slicing-constrained EDF scheduler serves users in each slice. Live validation: about 24% RU energy savings with per-slice satisfaction ratios of 0.94 and 0.95, outperforming ASM-only, slicing-only, and random baselines.

name: CORTEX · LLM-MLB
title: Experience-Guided LLM rApp for Mobility Load Balancing on ns-3/FlexRIC
authors: Jinhyeok Hwang, Hyeonji Hwang, Junhyeong Jo, Lingyan Bao, Youngpo Lee, and Jemin Lee
summary: LLM-empowered mobility load balancing with experience-guided policy generation for O-RAN. A Qwen-based analysis module uses Agent Evolution Manager (AEM)-retrieved experience to set load-reduction targets, while a deterministic decision module selects UE handovers. AEM ON/OFF comparison in ns-3/FlexRIC simulations, with web dashboard including policies, handover actions, cell loads, and UE information.

name: CORTEX · CORD
title: Co-Scheduling RAN and Edge AI on a Shared Accelerator
summary: AI-RAN brings baseband processing and AI inference onto the same edge hardware. CORD turns this sharing into cooperation: the RAN and the AI application each know what the other is doing, so radio processing stays on time and AI services stay responsive. The goal is a single edge platform that runs both reliably. Validated on a live OAI 5G SA testbed.

name: CORTEX · GPU-RAN Energy
title: Cross-Layer Energy Profiling and Baseline Power Modeling of a GPU-Accelerated RAN
summary: Cross-layer energy profiling of a GPU-accelerated RAN: an NVIDIA Aerial physical layer and an OAI higher-layer stack on a GB10 host with a physical radio unit. Application, MAC, PHY, scheduling, resource and power observations are aligned on common time support, separating RU AC, host AC and host DC power. Across 76 active runs and 8 no-iperf references, compact RAN-state models predict power more accurately than bidirectional-throughput baselines (RU AC RMSE 0.097 W vs 0.915 W), and the large running baseline sets the agenda for AI-RAN energy optimization.
